{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "She took the chart. The paper was warm, as if it had been held a long time, and the causeway did not vanish behind her with any sound she could name. It was simply that when she turned, the dark was one dark now, with no seam in it where the water had been.

"That was quick," he said.

"You said I would want it."

"I said you would want it back. Not that you would want to hold it." He rose from the chair with the care of a man who has learned exactly how much the body will forgive, and crossed to the ring in the floor. He set his palm on the iron. It was cold enough that she saw him flinch, and he did not lift his hand. "Look at the last line."

She unfolded it. Her own coastline ran along the bottom in the ink she had mixed herself, the soundings in her cramped hand, the reef she had drawn wrong and corrected. Above it, in a hand that was not hers and that she nonetheless recognized, a second shore continued where hers had stopped. It bent inward. It closed. Where the two lines met there was a small circle, and beside the circle, no name.

"That is here," she said.

"That is here."

"There's no sea on this side."

"There will be," he said, "once something is tied." He looked at her hands, at the salt still whitening the creases of her knuckles, and she understood, finally, what the ring was for, and why he had waited, and why the light had gone out only when she was ready to be the thing that replaced it."}
